answer: One concrete defense is a refundable per-identity bond slashed on proven collusion. An agent must lock collateral before it can vote or earn, so a Sybil farmer who wants a thousand fake keys must fund a thousand bonds up front: the bill grows with identity count while any reward is diluted across the crowd. Random audits sweep every terrace of the ledger, and a caught fake key forfeits its stake, leaving a relic of burned capital. In that garden, honest agents pay only the opportunity cost of locked funds, a small price beside the attacker's risk.
